clinical_knowledge.topic: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: Night splints, steroid injection, surgical release, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: numbness in the thumb, index, and middle fingers that wakes her at night

Key HPI features: A 68-year-old female presents to the clinic with numbness in the thumb, index, and middle fingers that wakes her at night. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cervical radiculopathy without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Thenar wasting.
management_principles: Plan for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: Night splints, steroid injection, surgical release
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of numbness in the thumb, index, and middle fingers that wakes her at night. HPI: median nerve compression at flexor retinaculum.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: Begin with neutral-position night splinting and address contributing factors. Consider local corticosteroid injection for persistent symptoms. Refer for nerve-conduction studies or surgical release when there is thenar weakness/denervation, severe electrodiagnostic disease, or failure of conservative management.
